Jordan — thanks for the draft. Quick legal guidance and three suggested copy options (short -> longer). High-level points first:

- Classification: we treat customer inputs/outputs as "Customer Content" in the DPA. Telemetry used for improving models or feature analytics is scoped as "Aggregated/Operational Telemetry" when it does not contain or identify Customer Content.
- Opt-out: hosted customers can opt out of telemetry-use-for-improvement via a console toggle or an account-level setting; opting out prevents use of request/response content for model training and feature analytics but does not disable necessary operational logs for debugging within the retention limits stated in the DPA.
- Subprocessors & transfers: we use a limited set of subprocessors (monitoring and metrics vendors, cloud infra). Transfers to the US are covered by Standard Contractual Clauses plus additional technical controls for logging partitions. We can/should include a link to the subprocessor list in the console.

Suggested copy: 

1) Short (button/tooltip): 

"We collect limited operational telemetry to run the service. You can opt out of sharing request/response data for product improvement in Settings. See DPA excerpt for details."

2) Medium (console privacy panel):

"Redwood collects operational telemetry (performance metrics, error traces, and system logs) to ensure reliability and improve the platform. By default, request and response content is not used for model training; customers can enable or disable telemetry-use-for-improvement in the Privacy settings. Essential logs required for debugging are retained for a short period as described in the DPA. Subprocessors and transfer safeguards (SCCs) are documented in our subprocessor list."

3) Legal-lite (for procurement):

"Operational telemetry collected includes aggregated performance metrics and system logs. Customer request/response content is designated as Customer Content in the DPA. Customers may opt out of allowing Redwood to use Customer Content for product improvement; such opt-out does not obviate operational logs necessary to maintain the service. Cross-border transfers to the U.S. are governed by SCCs and technical safeguards; a current subprocessor list is available on request or via the console."

I've attached a narrow redline of the DPA excerpt (section 3.c, telemetry & data uses) and flagged the retention window language we recommend keeping.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
